title: Hai Phong police warn that links to watch full AI films on Facebook and TikTok can be traps, GenK reports
summary: GenK reports that police of Ha Bac commune, Hai Phong (the article credits Hai Phong city police) warn that links offering the full version of AI films on Facebook and TikTok can be used to spread malware, take over accounts and take money from bank accounts. The article says the links are often placed in comments or posts. It states no figures or losses.
plain: Police in Hai Phong, Vietnam, warn that links to 'watch the full AI film' on Facebook and TikTok can be traps that spread malware and take over accounts or bank money.
exec: Hai Phong police warn that fake film links on social media can hijack accounts and bank money, as reported by GenK.
action: Hai Phong police advise not clicking strange links of unclear origin shared on social media, not giving OTP codes, passwords or bank details, and reporting a hacked account to the nearest police.
geo_basis: Hai Phong city police, the warning's source as stated by GenK
date_note: GenK gives only its publication day, 25 November, for the police warning.

validation.note: Only GenK read; the police's own notice was not read. CafeF, Soha and Nguoi Dua Tin carry the same story but were not opened.

review.note: surface changed from email-phishing to unknown (article describes social media links, not email); rest matches GenK
